As adults, individuals of this species reach a remarkable ultimate total length of 318 cm [Li = 318 cm], placing them among the larger, though not the largest, members of the family Pristidae. The species exhibits a notably slow pace of life, a common trait among elasmobranchs, which is reflected in its delayed onset of reproductive capability. Puberty is not attained until individuals reach a total length of approximately 280 cm [Lp = approximately 280 cm], a size that represents a significant proportion of their ultimate length. This life-history pattern makes the species highly reliant on the survival of adults and older juveniles, as they represent the demographic core of the population.
